item.description:
Settlers smash cars, damage ambulance in West Bank village

Israeli settlers smashed cars and hurled rocks at Palestinian residents of al-Mughayyir village in the occupied West Bank while Israeli forces looked on, according to a video shared by Palestinian rights activist Ihab Hassan on X.

Masked Israeli settler terrorists attacked the village of Al-Mughayyir in the West Bank today, in front of and under the protection of the Israeli border police. pic.twitter.com/iUMr72HIex

— Ihab Hassan (@IhabHassane) September 26, 2026

Israeli settlers, under the protection of Israeli forces, also attacked an ambulance and stole agricultural equipment during a raid on al-Mughayyir, northeast of Ramallah, on Saturday evening, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

Al-Mughayyir Village Council head Amin Abu Alia told Wafa that the settlers also raided a sheep farm west of the village and stole agricultural equipment.

During the attack, Israeli forces raided a house in the western part of the village, searched it and tampered with its contents. The forces also fired tear gas grenades in the area, with no injuries reported.

Abu Alia said Israeli forces also briefly detained several citizens, including women and children, at the village's western entrance and subjected them to mistreatment, before releasing them.

Israeli settler terrorists attacked a Palestinian ambulance while paramedics were trying to reach and treat people injured in a settler attack on the village of Al-Mughayyir in the West Bank. pic.twitter.com/2jI8T0qRvU

item.description:
Israel's attorney general orders postponement of E1 settlement tender

Israel’s attorney general has ordered a one-month postponement of an E1 settlement construction tender in the West Bank to avoid it being used for electioneering, Al Jazeera reported.

The tender, published on 18 August, covers seven residential compounds containing 1,234 housing units, out of the 3,401 units approved for E1, according to Israeli media. The deadline for bids had been set for 19 October, eight days before the Knesset election.

E1 (East 1) would link Ma’ale Adumim and other illegal Israeli settlements to occupied East Jerusalem, effectively severing the West Bank and disrupting Palestinian movement between the northern and southern West Bank, and isolating communities on each side.

The European Union has said the E1 settlement project fundamentally undermines the prospects for a two-state solution.

It noted that these developments come amid increasing instability in the West Bank and record levels of settler violence.

item.description:
US thanks Turkey, Oman, UAE for supporting sanctions against Iran

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has thanked the governments of the United Kingdom, Turkey, Oman and the UAE for supporting Washington’s "Operation Economic Outcast", a harsh economic campaign against Iran.

"At my direction, teams were dispatched across the globe to engage with countries and demand action against the Iranian regime," he said on X. 

 “These efforts are delivering results,” he wrote.

Bessent noted that Turkey and Oman have halted incoming flights from private carrier Mahan Air, while the United Arab Emirates has stopped all flights by Iranian airlines.

Dubai, the UAE's commercial hub, is a major destination for Iran's carriers, with multiple daily flights, a large Iranian community and close business links. Bessent also highlighted new banking restrictions.

On Wednesday, the UAE central bank blocked transactions to and from Iran by branches of Iran's Bank Melli, accusing it of violating laws on money laundering, terrorism and arms proliferation.

Last week, Turkey revoked the license of Iran's Bank Mellat, a semi-private financial entity that has been subject to Western sanctions for years.

“I appreciate the governments of the UK, Turkiye, Oman, and the UAE. We will continue working together as there is more to be done to prevent Tehran from carrying out its terrorist agenda,” Bessent wrote.

item.description:
Israeli police 'reopen' probe into pepper-spray attack on Armenian boy

Israeli police have reopened investigation into the pepper-spraying of a nine-year-old Armenian Christian boy in Jerusalem, after closing it despite the assault being capture on security cameras, according to Israeli journalist Yossi Eli.

"Following my exposé and the shock from what happened to William, the police have reopened the case and will collect the cameras. If this weren't so sad, it would be gratifying that the police only work like this," Eli wrote on X.

The boy, identified only as William, was riding his bicycle near the Mamilla neighbourhood on Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar, while listening to music through headphones.

A group of men approached him and demanded he remove his headphones, which he did. After hearing him speak English, one of the men said, "No English, Jews," before spraying him with pepper spray.

A video shared by Eli shows William seen crying inside an ambulance as his mother reassures him that his younger sister, Arev, is safe.

Eli reported that this was the second attack on William. In the first, he was accompanied by his father, who intervened to protect him; this time, he was alone.

item.description:
US-led coalition to withdraw from Iraq's Kurdistan by 30 September

US-led coalition forces are scheduled to withdraw from facilities in Iraq's Kurdistan region by September 30 under an agreement between Baghdad and Washington to wind down the coalition mission.

The move follows a series of military base handovers to Iraqi forces during 2025 and marks a key step in Iraq's transition to bilateral security arrangements with the United States.

 Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi told the United Nations General Assembly on Friday that the end of the international coalition's mission would move Iraq's relationship with its strategic partners from military cooperation to economic and development cooperation.

Zaidi urged all countries to tighten border controls, close gaps and remain vigilant against conditions that fuel extremism.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Riyadh schools to operate remotely for week, AFP reports
item.description:
Riyadh schools to operate remotely for week, AFP reports

Parents across Riyadh received emails from schools on Sunday announcing a last-minute plan to shift to remote learning for a week, according to messages seen by AFP.

"We have just been informed by Saudi authorities that schools must remain closed all week," read two separate messages seen by AFP. 

There was no official reason given but the move comes amid heightened tensions in the Gulf and near-daily attacks aimed at Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi fighters in Yemen.

"When a decision affects an entire school community for a full week, families deserve clear communication and transparency about the reasons behind it," one parent living in Riyadh who spoke on condition of anonymity told AFP. 

"It's a last-minute decision. We have no clue what's happening," a Lebanese expatriate living in Riyadh added.

The announcement comes a day after the Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted drones and ballistic missiles targeting the kingdom. 

The strikes were the latest in a series of escalating Houthi attacks since July, when renewed hostilities shattered a years-long truce and embroiled Yemen in the wider Middle East war.

The United Nations Security Council earlier condemned escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia by Houthi fighters, noting that the strikes have wounded "civilians, including women and children".

Report by AFP

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Iraq seeks US exemption from sanctions on Iranian airlines
item.description:
Iraq seeks US exemption from sanctions on Iranian airlines

The Iraqi government has said it is in talks with the United States to seek an exemption from sanctions on Iranian airlines, which have disrupted travel for patients, students and pilgrims.

All Iraqi airports enforced the US ban this week, resulting in major disruption at the airport serving the holy city of Najaf, the main destination in Iraq for Iranian flights.

"The Iraqi government is holding direct talks with the American side to exempt certain Iraqi airports from these measures," the prime minister's media office said.

An exemption, it added, would allow flights to resume "for humanitarian reasons, including medical treatment, education, religious visits, and for the interest of civilians".

Iranian airlines mainly carry Iraqi Shia pilgrims to Iran's holy cities or Iranians visiting sacred sites in Iraq. The flights also serve Iraqi students studying in Iran and patients seeking medical treatment there.

In an interview with Iranian news agency ISNA, Iran's ambassador to Iraq Mohammad Kazem Al-Sadegh said his country was also in contact with the Baghdad authorities to find a way to restore the flights.

"There are roughly 25 daily flights from Iran to Najaf and about 15 flights to Baghdad, and... around 12,000 to 13,000 people travel between Iran and Iraq and vice versa on Iranian airlines, which is not a small number," he said.

Report by AFP

“My decision is based purely on the belief the killing of innocent people is wrong,” Bazunu said in a statement posted on social media.

“Representing my country means everything to me,” Bazunu wrote. “I am a man of strong faith and try my best to be a person of morals and principles, therefore I feel that participating in the upcoming matches against Israel would be wrong.”

He added: “There are times when you have the opportunity to stand for a greater cause, and I strongly believe this is one of those moments.”

The Republic of Ireland will nevertheless play Israel in Sunday's Uefa Nations League match in Debrecen, Hungary, after the squad voted by a significant majority to proceed with the fixture, Football Association of Ireland CEO David Courell said Saturday.

The vote followed several hours of discussions at the team hotel over whether to boycott the game.

Ireland will wear black armbands during the match and will not shake hands with the Israeli players before kickoff, according to the report.
